title: Scary, Awkward-to-Use Grill Lacks On/Off Switch, Temperature Control
text:
Scary, Awkward-to-Use Grill Lacks On/Off Switch, Temperature Control. To only make grilled cheese sandwiches and panini, I thought this GEORGE FOREMAN 4-SERVING REMOVABLE PLATE GRILL AND PANINI PRESS (Black, GRP1060B) would be satisfactory for my needs. Wrong, wrong, wrong!

My grill arrived new in the box, and it didn’t smoke or smell bad when I followed the manufacturer’s instructions to start by heating it empty for 15 minutes (to burn off any manufacturing oil or residue). However, the budget-priced (about $29 on Amazon) grill is rather scary to use.

First, there is NO on/off switch or temperature control. The grill heats when you plug it in, and it gets VERY hot in about 5 minutes. You turn the grill off by unplugging it, and it takes quite a while to cool enough for you to remove the dishwasher-safe plates. At least the cord doesn’t heat up, and it doesn’t spark when you unplug it.

Second, the hinge, which “adjusts” to handle thicker or thinner items placed on the grill, is very clunky. When you open the lid and pull up, the hinge pulls up to make a wider space between the two grill plates. However, the hinge doesn’t pull evenly or all that easily.

Third, all of the black plastic parts (including the adjustable hinge) get hot when the grill is heated. You really need to handle this grill with oven mitts or hot pads.

Fourth, the electrical cord is extremely short--shorter than most “short cord” countertop appliances that use a short cord as a safety feature. Because the cord is so short, the cord won’t reach my kitchen countertop outlet unless I place the grill sideways on the countertop. This makes it awkward to load the grill, which is really designed to be opened from the front.

The worst of these four bad features is the lack of a temperature control. The only temperature is “very hot”, so it’s hard to toast grilled cheese sandwiches or panini sandwiches without burning them.

I wouldn’t dream of purchasing this grill for use in cooking meats or grilling vegetables. While the grill isn’t exactly flimsy, it is clear that the manufacturer has put the minimum amount of material into the grill’s manufacture. I’m pretty sure that the grill will burn out or quit working fairy soon if it is used at all regularly.
